name: Correlativa
description: Correlativa is a Mexican domino game in the trains family, related to Garrafina. Players build matching trains from a central double and, when blocked, draw from a boneyard until they can play or the boneyard is empty.

rules.objective: Play all your tiles first, or in a blocked position finish with the lowest remaining pip total.
rules.gameplay: Correlativa follows a train-style domino layout from a central opening double. Players extend legal train ends by matching pips. If a player cannot play, they draw one tile from the boneyard and continue drawing until they can play or the boneyard is exhausted. The deal ends when a player empties their hand or all players are blocked with no draw available.
keyRules: Tiles must match the exposed train end by pip value.
Blocked players draw from boneyard until playable or boneyard is empty.
Deal ends on a player going out or full block with no available draws.
Scoring is based on pip totals remaining in players' hands at deal end.

strategy.basic: Keep playable numbers flexible and avoid being forced to draw repeatedly from the boneyard.
strategy.intermediate: Track which numbers are nearly exhausted to guide safer plays and reduce block risk.
strategy.advanced: Steer branch ends toward numbers opponents are unlikely to hold while preserving your own exit routes.
tips: Use doubles to control train direction when the board is tight.
Protect low-pip exits for endgame to reduce blocked-hand penalties.
When ahead, prefer low-risk plays that preserve guaranteed matches.
